q6.answer: A's own fencing agent makes A read-only or stops it once its lease renewals have failed for longer than the lease length minus a safety margin, without waiting for the cloud. B promotes only after the witness lease has expired plus a clock-skew margin. The residual risk is a hung fencing agent with A's database still writable, which no lease scheme can stop, so the plan relies on drills.

q7.answer: The witness store, a small record in a third location outside both regions, is the authoritative record. The failover command writes it with a compare-and-set (active = B, epoch n+1) before promoting B, and A's primary renews its lease in it every 10 s. An old primary and A's fencing agent read it to compare epoch and timeline. The witness is not yet chosen or provisioned.

q8.answer: Jobs A had marked running before the last change that reached B show as running on B and are requeued after promotion. Jobs A marked done after that change show as unfinished on B and run again, and those completions are lost within the RPO window. Workers on A's cut-off network may still finish external work, and that effect cannot be undone, so requeue is safe only with real, tested idempotency keys per job and step.

q9.answer: Before the witness compare-and-set, an aborted run changes nothing and A stays primary, so the team can simply retry or go back. If the health check on B fails after promotion, DNS is not moved and the plan says to fix B and resume from that health check. The plan does not specify how the command resumes if it is interrupted between the compare-and-set and promotion. After promotion, A cannot return as primary (its epoch is stale), so returning to A requires a separate planned switchover after rebuilding A as a replica of B.

q10.answer: During the failover, DNS still points at A, so requests fail until B is up and passing its health check and DNS is moved. Clients with cached DNS then keep reaching A until the 60 s TTL expires, and some resolvers ignore TTL, so some users arrive later. Users who were signed in must sign in again, because Redis sessions are not replicated.

q11.answer: The plan has no hard bound on loss: replication is asynchronous, and the command's gate allows promotion only when replay lag is 30 s or less, unless the operator uses the accept-data-loss override. Replay lag cannot show changes A committed but never sent to B, so the LSN gap must also be checked, and the byte threshold for that gap is not yet set. Jobs completed inside the window are also lost and rerun.
